# Amos Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 335v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/AMO_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Listen to me, you fat cows of Bashan living in Samaria — you women who oppress the poor, crush the needy, and demand that your husbands keep the wine flowing!

**2** The Sovereign LORD has sworn this by his holiness: "The time will come when you will be dragged away with hooks — every last one of you hauled out with fishhooks! **3** You will be dragged through breaches in the wall, each of you going straight out, and you will be thrown out toward Harmon," declares the LORD.

**4** "Go ahead — keep going to Bethel and sin! Go to Gilgal and sin even more! Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days. **5** Offer your bread of thanksgiving and brag about your freewill offerings — shout about them to everyone! That's what makes you happy, isn't it, Israel?" declares the Sovereign LORD.

**6** "I sent you hunger in every city and famine in every town, but you still wouldn't come back to me," says the LORD. **7** "I held back the rain three months before harvest. I would send rain on one town but not on another. One field would get rain while another dried up. **8** People staggered from town to town looking for water but never had enough — and still you wouldn't come back to me," says the LORD.

**9** "I struck your farms with blight and mildew. I sent locusts to devour your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees — and still you wouldn't come back to me," says the LORD.

**10** "I sent plagues like the ones I sent against Egypt. I killed your young men in battle and let your horses be captured. I made the stench of dead bodies rise from your camps — and still you wouldn't come back to me," says the LORD.

**11** "I destroyed some of your cities the way I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. You who survived were like a burning stick snatched from a fire — and still you wouldn't come back to me," says the LORD.

**12** "Therefore, this is what I will do to you, Israel — and because I will do this to you: Prepare to meet your God!"

**13** For the one who formed the mountains, who creates the wind, who reveals his thoughts to mankind, who turns the dawn to darkness, and who treads the heights of the earth — the LORD God of Heaven's Armies is his name.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"Cows of Bashan" (v.1):** The most deliberately provocative opening in all of prophecy. Amos addresses the elite women of Samaria — dripping with wealth, demanding luxury — as fattened cattle. The insult is social commentary: these women drive the economy of oppression by demanding more from their husbands, who extract it from the poor.

**"Yet you did not return to me" (vv.6-11):** Five times. Famine. Drought. Crop failure. Plague. Near-destruction. Each time, the same heartbroken refrain. This is not a vindictive God gleefully punishing — it is a God exhausting every warning, every signal, every wake-up call, and watching his people sleep through all of them.

*— PNEUMA*
